title: Evidence of the implementation of a professional practice model and absenteeism and engagement indicators among the nursing team: A scoping review protocol
content:
by Wania Regina Mollo Baia, Isabela Gomes Musa dos Santos, Ricardo Toshio Yamassake, Vivian Aline Mininel, Renata Santos Tito, Patricia Campos Pavan Baptista

Objective

To map the evidence regarding the relationship between management and professional practice models and absenteeism and engagement indicators among nursing teams in healthcare services.

Introduction

The nursing workforce is the largest global workforce in healthcare; however, unequal distribution, high turnover, and absenteeism exist, directly impacting quality of care and patient safety. Professional practice models grounded in shared governance and participatory leadership have emerged as promising strategies to promote engagement and retention of these professionals. Nevertheless, the absence of systematic mapping as to how these models influence absenteeism and engagement justifies the development of this scoping review.

Eligibility criteria

Following the Participants, Concept, and Context (PCC) strategy, this review encompasses nursing teams working across different levels of healthcare complexity. The central concept investigates the relationship between Professional Practice Models (PPMs)—operationally defined as overarching frameworks incorporating shared governance and participatory leadership as core structural components—and indicators of engagement and absenteeism. The context encompasses public or private healthcare services that have implemented formal PPMs or organizational recognition programs.

Methods

This scoping review protocol is developed in accordance with the JBI methodological guidance and reported following the PRISMA-ScR checklist. Searches will be conducted in the PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. Additionally, grey literature will be included through searches of organizational websites and thesis and dissertation repositories. After removal of duplicates, two independent reviewers will screen titles and abstracts according to the eligibility criteria, followed by full-text assessment of the selected studies. Data extraction will be performed by two reviewers, and the results will be presented in tables, charts, and narrative summaries.
